exposure: genital malformations (Mullerian anomalies, external genital anomalies)
outcome: obstetric history (preterm births, mode of birth)
cohort: The study included 37 women with rectoperineal, rectovestibular, or cloacal fistulas (types of anorectal malformations) with a median age of 28 years (range 19-61 years).
finding: Women with anorectal malformations can achieve pregnancy irrespective of the type of ARM or presence of genital anomalies; 67% of those attempting pregnancy conceived successfully, mostly spontaneously, and carried to full term.
mod_finding: Among the 15 live births reported by women with ARM, 14 were delivered by Cesarean section, with only one vaginal delivery.
cross-section timing: Data was collected at a single point in time via questionnaires from women with ARM aged 19-61 years, regarding their past reproductive and obstetric history.
